messages:
jamie: Heads up — us-west2 preemptible eviction rate just spiked (~3x) over the last 10m, mixed-capacity pools are losing nodes and queues are growing. Anyone around?

sree: I'm oncall, looking now. Which pool and which workloads?

jamie: mixed-ml-gpu-pool-us-west2, mostly text-gen routes. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/ML/preemptible-signals?orgId=1 :eyes:

liam: Quick numbers: eviction_score went from ~0.02 -> 0.09, interruption_rate(5m)=0.14, preemptible_capacity_remaining dropped below 15% for several AZs.

ana: tagging to note SLO impact: p95 latency for /v1/generate jumped 120ms -> 250ms in affected shard.

sree: short-term mitigations: 1) shift overflow to on-demand for critical lanes, 2) lower preemptible max_burst to prevent cascading evictions, 3) shepherd traffic to eu-west1 canary.

jamie: +1 to overflow but we should gate it behind an SLO-impact check to avoid cost surprises.

liam: proposed PromQL probe for alert correlation:

```
sum(rate(preemptible_evictions_total[5m])) / sum(preemptible_capacity_total)
AND
avg_over_time(textgen_queue_depth[5m]) > 20
```

sree: will open PR to change alerting rule to fire only when both eviction_ratio > 0.05 sustained for 5m AND queue_depth condition true. That should cut flapping alerts.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-453 created for preemptible instability in us-west2 (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-453)

liam: also adding SLO delta to critical alert: if p95 latency delta > 10% for 5m, mark as critical and auto-trigger fallback policy.

jamie: fallback policy should prefer hedging before full on-demand fallback: 1) rebalance pool weights to more stable regions, 2) open small dedicated capacity (scale +10%), 3) if still failing, enable on-demand overflow.

ana: cost note: full on-demand fallback across affected stacks ~+$12k/day. Hedging (rebalance + small ded) ~+$2.5k/day. Documented in ticket.

sree: I'll update runbook with steps + add a short playbook script to adjust pool weights and toggle overflow. PR 5423 created (alert + runbook draft). Assigning to eng-infra.

liam: test plan: canary 10% traffic to fallback in eu-west1, verify KV cache warmup within 2 deploys, measure p95 and error rate.

jamie: small config snippet for alert change (will put in PR):

```yaml
- alert: PreemptibleEvictionSustainedWithQueue
  expr: (sum(rate(preemptible_evictions_total[5m])) / sum(preemptible_capacity_total)) > 0.05
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained preemptible evictions with queue growth"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/preemptible-hedging"
```

ana: also let's add a derived metric 'preemptible_health_index' that folds eviction rate, capacity remaining, and network packet drops. Could use anomaly detection to flag noisy signals.

sree: agreed. I'll wire an MFA for ops to approve on-demand overflow if cost estimate > $5k/day.

opsbot: deploy-bot: PR 5423 merged to staging, alert rule updated.

jamie: nice — after staging validation, promote to prod and then run the canary. Please post here when prod deploy done. :thumbsup:

liam: noted. I'll run the canary tonight at 23:00 UTC and post metrics.

jamie: thanks everyone. Keeping the thread as the source of truth for this incident and follow-ups.
